Name: Open Source Intelligence
Definition: Intelligence derived from publicly available information that is collected, processed, and used under applicable policy and law.
Example: Public weather alerts and media reports used in a crisis brief
Classification Notes: Use does not remove privacy, licensing, or policy obligations

Name: Publicly Available Information
Definition: Information that has been published or broadcast for public access, made available by request, or otherwise lawfully accessible to the public.
Example: A public port authority disruption bulletin
Classification Notes: Public availability does not imply unrestricted reuse

Name: Source Reliability Score
Definition: A steward-reviewed score representing historical accuracy, timeliness, correction history, and corroboration behavior for a source.
Example: An official bulletin source has SRS 96

Name: Corroboration Count
Definition: Number of independent source families supporting the same event or signal.
Example: Three unrelated public sources report a port closure
Classification Notes: Higher count improves confidence but does not guarantee truth

Name: Analytic Confidence
Definition: Assessment of how strongly available evidence supports an analytic judgment.
Example: High confidence that a road closure is active
Classification Notes: Should be explainable through provenance and source quality

Name: Mission Purpose
Definition: Documented reason for requesting and using a data product.

Name: Handling Caveat
Definition: Use restriction or instruction attached to a data asset or product.
Example: Aggregated use only; no individual profiling

Name: Purpose Limitation
Definition: Requirement that data be used only for the stated and approved purpose.
Example: Use approved for crisis brief, not unrelated investigations

Name: License Restriction
Definition: Limit imposed by source terms, contract, or policy on redistribution, citation, retention, or use.
Example: Article metadata may be stored, but full text may not be redistributed
Classification Notes: Track at asset and field level

Name: Source Citation
Definition: Reference back to the originating public source or approved source registry entry.

Name: Aggregation Level
Definition: Spatial, temporal, or logical level at which records are summarized.
Classification Notes: Higher aggregation can reduce privacy risk

Name: No Raw Personal Data
Definition: Classification indicating that the product excludes raw person-level records and direct personal identifiers.

Name: Sensitive Analytic Inference
Definition: Governance flag for outputs that may reveal conclusions, risk judgments, or patterns requiring review even when input data is public.
Classification Notes: Often requires purpose and audience controls

Name: Data Product
Definition: Packaged, reusable data asset with context, owner, quality expectations, access method, and usage guidance.
Classification Notes: Marketplace-ready when ownership and controls are complete

Name: Lineage
Definition: Trace of how data moves from sources through transformations to consumption.
Example: Source Registry -> Ingestion -> Review -> Curated Feed
